key_insight: Combining freeway-wide traffic measurements with sparse connected-vehicle observations lets deep reinforcement learning make better ramp-metering decisions under partial observability.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce congestion, travel time, and spillback at on-ramps, making it relevant for real-world freeway traffic control systems with limited sensor coverage.
method: Encode macroscopic traffic state plus a two-channel grid of connected-vehicle presence and speed.
Use a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network to choose ramp-metering green durations.
Train and test in SUMO across varying demand levels and CV penetration rates.
evidence_signal: Across 50 matched scenarios, the hybrid controller reduced total travel time by 11.4% and mean spillback duration by 84.9% versus ALINEA, with an additional ~1.6% travel-time gain under full CV visibility.
watch_item: Performance depends on CV penetration and reliable observation encoding, so results may weaken in low-connectivity deployments or when sensor/CV data are noisy.
paper_title: Ramp Metering Control via Hybrid State Deep Reinforcement Learning in Partially Observable Connected Vehicle Environments
